articleTitle: A Vision Module for Visually Impaired People by Using Raspberry PI Platform
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper describes a vision based platform for real-life indoor and outdoor object detection in order to guide visually impaired people. The application is developed using Python and functions from OpenCV library and, ultimately ported upon Raspberry PI3 Model B+ platform. Template Matching is selected as method. More precisely, a multi-scale version approach is proposed to reduce the processing time and also to extend the detection distance range for accurate traffic sign recognition in indoor/outdoor environment. The experimental part addressed the finding of the optimum values for template and image source dimension, as well as the scaling factor.

articleTitle: Automatic Number Plate Recognition for a Smart Service Auto
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: There is a growing need to use technology when it comes to consumers. Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) is a system that allows real time recognition of a vehicle license number plate. For a smart service auto, ANPR is helping promoting development, personalizing classic application and increasing productivity for clients and workers. The main role of ANPR, in the application, is to extract the characters of a vehicle license number plate from an image. A smart car service brings in addition to other services, an application through which the customer can see the repairs of the vehicle using only the license plate number extracted from a loaded image. It has been noticed that the technological development is growing, so it is considered that there is a need for development in this field too, and a smart car service is the best option for car services. By using ANPR to develop an application, it can ease the work of many employees as well as clients of car services.

articleTitle: Efficient IoT system for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The introduction of automation and telemetry systems in precision agriculture is an innovative approach that could conduct to the implementation of an information system that can provide data on irrigation during all year. Climate change and population growth contribute to a multitude of problems in agriculture and have an impact on farming practices. The need for an automation and telemetry system for irrigation is emphasized by the market's interest in having access to fully automated monitoring and automation solutions for energy-efficient and cost-effective agricultural crops. The advantages of system architecture presented in this paper consist in very low energy consumption, low management costs, scalability, forecasting functions, diagnosis, enlargement facility lead to an important technical impact and high potential for marketing. The aim of this paper is to use an integrated automation and telemetry solution in precision agriculture, taking into consideration the energy efficiency criteria and the latest technologies available on the market.

articleTitle: Development of an Automated System to Monitor and Control a Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Climate change brings a multitude of problems related to people's food resources. This resource must be protected and one of the solutions is to cultivate fruits and vegetables in closed spaces. It is also necessary to optimize the water consumption and reduce the human factor. The proposed automated system aims at monitoring and controlling the greenhouse regarding the temperature, humidity, carbon dioxide and other factors that influence plant growth.

articleTitle: The Induction Machine Operating from a Voltage Supply, Unbalanced and Polluted with Harmonics: A Practical Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper the authors applied analytical, and experimental procedures for investigating the operation of the three-phase induction motor (IM) energized from an unbalanced voltage supply and in the presence of harmonics. The main direction of investigation focuses on motor performance. The analytical model of the IM includes the effects of the voltage unbalance through the presence of positive and negative sequence parameters, as well as the effects of harmonics. The model takes into account the skin effect due to the presence of the higher frequency harmonics. The overall procedure proven to deliver a complete mapping of the IM operation, including the calculation of the unbalanced current, all categories of loss, developed torque, as well as the assessment of the harmonic effects. The final result of the work becomes useful in regards to IM rerating for the reason of preserving its lifespan.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Smart Cars Model for Autonomous Vehicles in a Platooning
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper presents a new car model prototype design which can be driven in platooning. After each part is tested in real time separately they are then integrated together to obtain the car system prototype and the C++ language is used to program the hardware component system to do its mission. This controls the car behavior which is developed in a real-time operating system as if it can become an autonomous vehicle for navigation purposes capable of avoiding collision as well as keeping a safe distance from the vehicle ahead on the road. The experimental results show the efficiency of this car model we developed. Further, the implementations on each car are made at low-cost, a fact which represents an advantage.

articleTitle: Software and hardware solutions for Using the keyboards by blind people
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper are presented some hardware and software solutions for the blind people. Only in Bucharest, the capital of Romania, there are over 6000 blind people, and the number of people with acute vision problems is much higher. There are software applications designed to help these people in their daily lives. With today's advanced technology, there are smartphones, tablets, or personal computer (PC) smartphone applications that help the blind persons for traveling and reading information. The software applications proposed in this article are useful for people with visual impairments in order to learn how to use a PC keyboard. The hardware device proposed can be a solution for learning to use a 3×4 numeric keypad by blind person.

articleTitle: Decontamination, Drying and Sterilization Assisted by the High Frequency Electromagnetic Field for the Processing of Construction Waste Used on Driveways
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper a series of laboratory tests were made using the high-frequency electromagnetic field to decontaminate, dry and sterilize of demolition materials as well as to determine physical properties and performance of demolition materials to see their potential use. This article examines the use of materials resulting from the demolition of concrete waste byproducts as a new source of building materials used in road construction. The amount of construction waste grows each year, while natural rocks are becoming more and more expensive. Recycled concrete from various sources, such as construction and demolition waste, is a good option that can be used as a foundation for road construction. The experimental results demonstrate that the materials in the selected concrete waste are suitable for use as base layers and flexible pavement substrates in road construction.

articleTitle: Impact of saturation and cross-saturation on SynRM's dynamic model
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper presents the impact that parameter estimation methods have on dynamic models used in control for synchronous reluctance machines (SynRM). The main parameters that will be analyzed are the d- and q-axis inductances. Also, saturation and cross-saturation phenomena and the impact of taking them into account when developing a dynamic model of a SynRM are studied. The SynRM considered for this analysis was designed with optimized flux-barriers shapes. For the dynamic model of the machine, Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) strategy will be used.

articleTitle: Hamming Code Performance Evaluation using Artificial Neural Network Decoder
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: With the increase in the connectivity among various electronic devices day-by-day, the technology has stepped up into a new era of Internet-of-Things. To ensure the accuracy, integrity and fault-tolerance in the transmitted data, Error Correcting Codes are used. Various techniques are available to decode the received data and correct the errors. In this paper, an approach based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) is been used to decode the received data because of their real-time operation, self-organization and adaptive learning. Back propagation Algorithm for feed forward ANN has been simulated using MATLAB for (7, 4) Hamming Code. The synaptic weights are updated during each training cycle. The designed ANN is trained for all possible combination of code words such that it can detect and correct 1-bit error. The Bit Error rate performance of the proposed ANN based method is compared with the syndrome decoding.

articleTitle: Segmenting Users of an Online Store Using Data Mining Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: An efficient marketing strategy is based on the proper analysis of the data collected from the history of the transactions made. The large amount of data is explored with data mining techniques, which permit the segmentation of customers depending on certain criteria. In this paper we have adopted one of the most widespread analysis process and applied it as a case study to a small business consisted of an online store.

articleTitle: Frequency Domain Models for Nonlinear Loads with Firing Angle control Devices Part I - Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Some measurements results aimed to be used to build frequency domain models for nonlinear loads containing thyristors are presented. Following similar procedures to those in our previous papers, the modules and phases dependences on the parameters of the fundamental voltage component are measured for all significant harmonic components of the currents. These results are given for a one thyristor rectifier and a three phase rectifier with three thyristors.

articleTitle: The Development of an Autonomous Maze Robot
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a robot capable to navigate through a simple maze, based on algorithms for maintaining the trajectory, making turns and finding the exit from the maze. Once we have been able to create such a robot, expanding the robot by adding new functionalities leads to its transformation, for example into a room vacuum cleaner, or why not, if the environment is a labyrinth, in a tool capable of determining the shortest route from any two points of the labyrinth. Its dimensions allow exploration of spaces inaccessible to humans. Robots of this kind are based on decision making algorithms, of which we mention the wall tracking algorithm and the flood fill algorithm. The robot presented is based on the wall tracking algorithm running on a microcontroller. This robot is made up of a printed circuit board that also has the role of chassis, two DC gear motors with incremental encoders, six distance sensors and a battery.

articleTitle: A Practical Approach of Design and Construction of a 100A Welding Inverter
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents and explains in depth how a low power welding inverter works and how the output current can be controlled through a primary current sensing circuit. During the entire design process, it was kept in mind to use as general and widely available components as possible both for simplicity and cost reduction and at the end it became a robust proof of concept.

articleTitle: Application of a Probabilistic Model to High Frequency Spectrum Occupancy
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Spectrum occupancy measurements and statistical models for spectrum occupancy data have been subject of interest since many years and are important as the spectrum becomes more and more crowded. Even with the unexpected growth of mobile communications, High Frequency (HF) radio links have advantages that make them unique in some application areas, justifying the development of spectrum occupancy models for the HF domain. In this paper a bidimensional Markov model for spectrum occupancy in HF is presented. The model takes into account both the time dimension and the frequency dimension one. The model is validated using real HF data acquired in the western part of Romania, using a Universal Software Radio Peripheral and a HF antenna. The spectrum occupancy values have been computed off-line for a set of frequency bands according to ITU frequency allocation. The results confirm the validity of the bidimensional Markov model as a useful tool to capture the statistical properties of spectrum occupancy in HF domain.

articleTitle: Neural Network Modeling of a Drying Process in Radio Frequency Field
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this study, a neural network model was developed and tested to predict the characteristics of a possible industrial wood processing based on electromagnetic technologies. The application presented in this paper is a drying process for a half-finished oak blanks exposed in a radiofrequency electromagnetic field. To develop the model of this process, MATLAB's Neural network toolbox was used. The drying process was simulated with the help of FEM-BEM.3D-RFmove _term_masa software and the simulation results were used then for the training of the proposed neural network. The trained neural network is effective to provide the process characteristics with good accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low Power Induction Heater
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper is focused on the practical realization of a low power induction heater with widely available components, for the purpose of studying the phenomena of heating using electromagnetic fields and the way to generate it.

articleTitle: Development and testing of a mixed feedback control system for robotic hand exoskeleton
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper research and development of a control system for a robotic hand exoskeleton is presented. The application area for the device is medical rehabilitation therapy. Application specific electronics are designed and implemented in the mechatronic system of a robotic exoskeleton. A comprehensive study is elaborated utilizing data generated by the exoskeleton during operation with and without the human hand interfaced in the device.

articleTitle: Challenges of developing mobile versions for high performance desktop VR applications
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper, we present our work on mobile version of a high performance desktop VR application. We analyze the available mobile VR solutions, and mobile hardware, and the limitation of the mobile platforms.

articleTitle: Fingerprint Authentication for Budget Application
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Security has become an increasingly popular domain in computer science. Because today devices are attacked not only by classical viruses but also intentional attacks occur, in order to stole data from devices and obtain material benefits, it is necessary to add new security types. These new ways of securing applications include technologies such as facial recognition, iris recoil, fingerprint recognition. Fingerprint algorithms have been embedded in modern mobile devices, for authentication. Nowadays mobile devices use a fingerprint scanner, so fingerprinting algorithms are becoming more widespread. This paper presents a fingerprint authentication algorithm based on the Advance Encryption Standard (AES) and on the Android Keystore System. The proposed algorithm is tested, by integrating it into a budget application.

articleTitle: Traffic signal controller implemented through a virtual instrument
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper, we present a solution for the implementation of a traffic light controller for an intersection which is realized as a virtual instrument obtained by LabVIEW programming. The hardware structure is accomplished by using a low-cost NI USB 6501 module. The controller assumes the equal traffic density on all the fourth directions on the intersection.

articleTitle: Inspection Robot for Tightly and Hard to Reach Spaces
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: When a disaster occurs, such as an earthquake, a robot crawling through the disaster areas arrives more and more, helping firefighters and rescue teams to work more securely. Such a robot crawling through the disaster areas for inspection is the snake robot. This paper presents the designing of a segmented snake robot to inspect narrow and hard-to-reach volumes. Snake robots can use their many internal degrees of freedom to thread through tightly packed volumes accessing locations that people and machinery otherwise cannot use. Finally, after designing, the command and control of this special robot are presented.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of the Analog and Digital Operation for Miniature Railway Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper we will present a comparative study of the analog and digital operation of miniature railway systems. Both operation modes are largely used for the operation of miniature model trains, and each one has its own advantages and disadvantages. Modern miniature trains, also known as “model trains”, are now designed and built with state-of-the-art technologies. Due to their very complex internal structure, the model trains are to be treated as miniature robots and to be operated with great care, according to their specific requirements. It is possible to use the analog system with digital trains and vice versa, but it is advised to avoid such situations in order to attain optimal operation and experience.

articleTitle: Experimental Identification of the 13C Isotope Separation Process by Cryogenic Distillation on a Two-Column Separation Cascade
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper presents the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C isotope separation cascade by cryogenic distillation of carbon monoxide at 81 K. It shows the performance of the columns separations for the total reflux (zero production) and feed regimes. The separation process was identified by drawing the most probable curvesfor the variation of the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C concentration over time, the time constant and the corresponding transfer function were determined. The transfer function obtained, which is proportional and of the first order, can be used for controlling and operating the separation cascade at full reflux or during production mode.

articleTitle: Bond-graph modeling of an electric thermogenerator
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to use the bond-graph modeling to analyze the characteristics of the equivalent electric circuit of an electric thermo-generator. This model will can be integrated in systems for solar energy recuperation. These systems can be also modeled and analyzed using the bond-graph models.

articleTitle: Control Methods for Five Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper are presented two control methods for single-phase five level inverter: staircase modulation (SM) and pulse width modulation (PWM). In both cases the switching sequences have been chosen so that the number of semiconductor devices which switch at a certain time to be minimal. For the PWM modulation, it has been studied how the arrangement of the carrier signals influences the total harmonic distortion factor (THD). The chosen switching sequences ensures voltages balancing on the inverter capacitors.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The aim of this study is to present the development and validation of a parameterized model for electromagnetic analysis of a surface permanent magnet synchronous machine (SPMSM) used for automotive applications. The model is developed based on the MATLAB - FEMM (Finite Element Method Magnetics) co-simulation, followed by the coupling between FEMM and LMS. Imagine AMESim software in order to extend the analysis at sub-system level, including the effect of power electronics.

articleTitle: Autonomous Line Maze Solver Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is steadily growing, especially nowadays. It starts to represent a necessity for various technological processes such as the automation of operations in various factories, certain robots that can make decisions without human help, cars that can drive alone. In this paper we present an application of artificial intelligence, namely a problem that is common in the field of robotics: navigating a robot in a labyrinth without human interaction, using the left hand rule and dead -end filling. The line maze solver using these algorithms will be able to drive through a labyrinth that has a solution and more precisely a “disk”. The robot uses a Raspberry Pi 3 as a “brain”, where with the Python 2 programming environment we have managed to implement these algorithms to solve our problem.

articleTitle: The Role of Susceptors in the Process of, Obtaining Nanopowders Using Microwaves
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents results of the 3D numerical modelling of an applicator used for the production of nanopowders. The role and effect of susceptible materials in microwave field processing and the influence of the thickness of insulators on the field distribution were analysed.

articleTitle: Information Analytics System Database for Uniform Approach to Continuous Engineering Program Improvement
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The Graduate Attribute Information Analysis System (GAIA) developed at the University of Ottawa to support the use of assessment data analytics for ongoing improvement of students' performance and continuous program development was successfully implemented in the Fall of 2015. Since then GAIA serves three engineering programs - Computer, Electrical and Software Engineering programs at the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science. GAIA stores and processes assessment data since 2012 and generates systematic assessment reports at program and departmental levels. In this paper we discuss current system modifications that allow for developing of a uniform approach towards data collection, analysis and reporting for the three programs. We introduce the Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) processes in place for assessing common graduate attributes. A special attention is given to the data transformation processes supporting two special purpose reports: Graduate Attribute Report per Cohort (GAR/C) and Course Progression Report per Cohort (CPR/C). The former shows average graduate attribute assessment data per each attribute, while the latter tracks student achievements as students progress within the program. Both reports are simultaneously generated per program. The fine data granularity allows for ETL interaction among sustainable data marts within the main assessment database. In this context, we outline the different stages of data processing leading to a uniform approach to continuous engineering program improvement. The described approach of assessment data management supports engineering accreditation, informs continuous program development and adds to the historic data trend analysis at program and faculty level. Furthermore, it allows for generation of COOP Progress Reports per cohort (COOPR/C).

articleTitle: Indoor localization method based on the sound signal - an Experimental Setup
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Indoor localization is a not too easy task for autonomous mobile robots, especially if a good precision is required. This task has the purpose to find another robot or to accomplish together complex tasks with one or more robots within the team. This paper presents an indoor localization method of a leader robot by the other robots in the team based on the sound signal emitted by it.

articleTitle: Semantic Similarities for Projects and Freelancers Profile Matching
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: People are more and more willing to become free-lancers and manage their personal projects. They hunt projects they can work at from home and for a short period of time. There are few portals that offer a richer filtering. Our application comes with a new approach, in order to offer a more appropriate filtering depending on each persons preferences. For that, our approach compares the data between the freelancer profile and the offered project, through a set of input parameters. These parameters are the skill, profession area and description. Texts are compared using semantic analysis, and the final score is displayed at the end of the process in the user interface.

articleTitle: Using S Parameters in Two-Port Circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The subject of this paper is a practical example where the application of the scattering parameters (SP) results in the active power transfer efficiency increase. The process of information transmission (propagation) improves, also. The efficiency assessment addresses the transfer function of a two-port network. The computation of the maximum power transferred to the load requires the application of the maximum active power transfer theorem. Furthermore, the results obtained applying the electric circuit theory are compared to those obtained through the S parameters method. Moreover, utilizing the SP is possible to determine the characteristic parameters of analog filters. In this way it is possible to compute the stop and pass frequency bands and classify the nature of the filters. In the domains of high and very high frequencies, SP can be easily measured using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). The SP offers an attractive procedure to solve linear circuits operating in the sinusoidal regime, with direct reference to multi-poles. Finally, simulation results regarding all of the above mentioned parameters have been compared with data obtained either experimentally or from literature.

articleTitle: Obtaining SiO2 Nanopowders Using Microwave Field Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper, experimental results regarding the obtaining of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanopowders of various sizes depending on the specific processing conditions and separation methods using microwaves are presented.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Microwave Field and Hot Air Drying of Barley Seeds
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The purpose of these experiments was to find optimum conditions based on the influence of microwave / hot air heating on barley seeds with high humidity. Parameters variation, temperature, humidity, power in the drying process were analyzed. The effects of microwaves on the drying characteristics were studied in two cases: the first case uses a constant microwave power and hot air jet at 55°C±10%, without taking into account the maximum allowable temperature in the seedbed, and in the second situation, variable power is used to ensure that the temperature does not exceed 65°C. The experiments were carried out on barley seeds, the Thuringia variety. To see and study the influence microwaves have on microwave field treated seeds, in the two above-mentioned cases, barley grains were germinated and the daily progression of the germination process was followed.

articleTitle: Frequency Correlated Filtering for Ambulatory Electrocardiograms
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Medical tendencies target nowadays at miniaturization and portability of noninvasive diagnosis devices. Analyzed signals captured outside the clinical environment are sensitive to external interferences and noise. A method based on the frequency dependence of the signal has been developed. The algorithm analyzes electrocardiogram data using wavelets and an exponentially growing thresholding algorithm. The results are promising and display after denoising more accurate electrocardiogram features.

articleTitle: Extraction of Volatile Pumpkin Oils through Cold Pressing versus Microwave Field -Features, Composition and Differences
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper refers to the extraction of pumpkin seed oil using two processes, namely the extraction of volatile oils by cold pressing and hot pressing, and in the last process it will be pointed out the extraction of volatile oils using microwaves. Pumpkin seeds will be selected, each experimental sample will be weighed, and, from the observed samples thus obtained, we will notice the physicochemical properties of the extracted oil. To avoid the occurrence of phenomena that would affect the integrity of the microwave generator, the system will operate in pulses using an adjustable power magnetron.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Cryptographic Strength of the LSB Steganographic Method with Pixel Sieving
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper an enhancement is proposed for the LSB (Least Significant Bits) type steganographic method based on the pixel sieve cryptographic primitive. The novelty of the method, the added security, resides in the fact that the useful data is hidden not in one digital image, but in several carrier images. To reconstruct the original data not only all the carrier images are required, but also the correct “encryption key” used to spread the data in the shares.

articleTitle: Risk assesment parameters for Internet of Things projects
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper was written in order to explain why a risk assessment algorithm will be useful for us to estimate the resources involved in an Internet of Things project. During my experience, I faced different challenges when building this kind of projects. It was very difficult to estimate the complexity of projects and the amount of resources used to build them. Being able to have an early overview over IoT projects will ease the processes involved in understanding the needs of such a project. As a quick overview, this paper will present the risk algorithm parameters, how to build the algorithm itself based on them and the general architecture of the application. If a project manager wants to assess and discuss a future project, an application like this will come in handy.

articleTitle: Extension of Mpdx Matrix for Upper Order Partial Diferential Equations with Two Independent Variables and Approximating Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents a case study for a (PDE n·m) system that includes three partial derivative equations of order n=2, n=4, n=6 with the same m=2 independent variables, time (t) and propagation space (s). In order to solve this (PDE n·m) system with approximating solutions, the Matrix of Partial Derivatives of the State Vector (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pdx</sub>) method is used. After computing the (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pdxA</sub>), (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pdxB</sub>) and (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pdxC</sub>) matrices, the numerical simulation becomes well systematized.

articleTitle: Predicting Solar Insolation and Energy Harvest of PV Modules in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Recently, energy consumption has increased worldwide. In Saudi Arabia, total generation capacity reached about 74.3 GW in 2016. This increasing demand of electrical energy in addition to other factors such as environmental challenges being faced by the world and increasing oil prices have all led to the increasing use of Renewable Energy Resources (RERs). Consequently, Saudi Arabia aims to use Photovoltaic (PV) extensively in the generation of electricity in the near future, both in utility scale and residential scale. In this paper, the insolation and energy delivered from residential scale PV modules will be assessed in different cities within Saudi Arabia. Simulation tool will be used for this purpose.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Fuzzy Approach of Stochastic Events Impact on Dependable Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The dependable systems behaviour builds the establishment for trustworthiness in any significant achievements in the information society. The dependability of a system is endangered if faults and failure in components of the system occur, being the cause for errors which can lead to consequent failure. Unexpected events, unavailability of equipment, instantaneous component failures, stoppage of automated equipment are unacceptable accidents that increasingly impacting the quality of life of persons and the quality of services in global society. The paper proposes a framework to evaluate the unavailability of the dependable systems using Fuzzy Multi-Stage Analysis. The method examines the importance factors of modelled system and the scenarios which can develop as a result of incidence of multiple, discrete events. The case of study, developed for realtime, operational conditions, validates, analytically, experimentally and by simulation, the efficiency of proposed method.

articleTitle: Production of Silicon Carbide in a High Frequency Electromagnetic Field. Measuring Thermal Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Materials like alumina and silicon carbide, sensitive to high frequency electromagnetic field are very useful for processing other materials in the high frequency electromagnetic field. The use of these sensitive materials can enhance a more uniform temperature alignment over a hot material in a high frequency electromagnetic field. These silicon carbide composites will be loaded with enriched cement. In this article, we will also discuss the factors that influence the heating rate of composed materials. These factors depend on the size of the silicon carbide particles, the percentage of silicon carbide in the volume of the composite material, the treatment atmosphere and the maximum experimental temperature. The heating rate of the composite materials was determined as the amount of silicon carbide increased while the heating rate increased. The size of the silicon carbide particles also influenced the heating rate of the composite material, which has been demonstrated experimentally. Mathematical model has shown that the effect of particle size is a geometric one dependent on a non-perfect thermal contact between the silicon carbide particle and the cement patern. The size of the silicon carbide particles also affected the filtration threshold of the composite materials. The heating rate of the composite materials grew when the calcium carbonate in the cement was pyrolyzed to form calcium oxide due to an growth in thermal conductivity.

articleTitle: About the Use of High Frequency Ceramic Susceptors for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper presents the possibility of using susceptible ceramics made of silicon carbide in industrial applications. In this sense it is showed that is possible to achieve very fast high temperature by using susceptible ceramics in microwave aplications. The experiments were carried out on two types of ceramic susceptors made from silicon carbide mixed with kaolin and different binders., in order to point out there behavior in microwave field. A mathematical model used to predict its behavior in high frequency field is also presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of Contact Resistance Variation in Electric Devices Under Electric Charge
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper presents a study regarding electric contacts conductivity, from the structure of certain types of electric devices, during their functioning under electric charge. The variation of the contact resistance, according to the structural changes of the contact surface is taken into study. The structure of the contacts surface was analyzed by microscopy.

articleTitle: Authentication and Recognition, Guarantor for on-Line Security
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: ARGOS is a web service we implemented to offer face recognition Authentication Services (AaaS) to mobile and desktop (via the web browser) end users. The Authentication Services may be used by 3rd party service organizations to enhance their service offering to their customers. ARGOS implements a secure face recognition-based authentication service aiming to provide simple and intuitive tools for 3rd party service providers (like PayPal, banks, e-commerce etc) to replace passwords with face biometrics. It supports authentication from any device with 2D or 3D frontal facing camera (mobile phones, laptops, tablets etc.) and almost any operating systems (iOS, Android, Windows and Linux Ubuntu).

articleTitle: Real Time Determination of Instantaneous Power Flow from Three-phase Electrical Circuits in Nonsymmetric Situations by Using ACE2000
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In three-phase electrical circuits (distribution electrical networks for alimentation with electrical energy), the non-symmetric situation may be characterized by the existence of negative and zero symmetric order components of the current, which have a bad influence on the efficiency of energy. One of the explanation is the instantaneous power flow of negative and zero components, as it is analyzed and explained in this paper. On symmetric situation, only the positive sequence component exists. Finally some simulation results are presented and also the experimental values, which were measured with ACE2000 device in electrical station for trams supplying trams with electrical energy.

articleTitle: General Considerations for Realizing a New Subclass of SoC
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper the mathematical calculations and the resulting mathematical model proposal of a real System-on-Chip (rSoC) will be presented, accommodating all the four main parts of any modern computer: microprocessor, volatile memory (e.g. RAM), non-volatile memory (e.g. Flash), and also the Input-Output (IO) controller. These parts could be realized in a cost-effective and simplistic manner only on one piece of silica die instead of several specialized Integrated Circuits (ICs) connected on the printed circuit board (PCB). The mathematical calculus is based on the approximate transistor count of already existing older ICs and architectures, which could be reused in this foreseen extremely cheap, scalable and, most importantly, implantable system.

articleTitle: Pulsed Electric Field Treatments for Improving the Colour of Red Grape Products
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental study of the application of PEF on Pinot Noir and Merlot grapes, in order to extract compounds that are responsible for the colour of grape products.

articleTitle: Numerical Images Analyze for Quality Control
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper define and describes a method about images processing, (more exactly: detection and inspection), in order to determine the correct number of pills, in the packing, and it ensure that the pills have the correct color. In this purpose, it was used LabView, National Instruments Vision Development Module and Irfanview software.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Process of Tempering a Semifinished Product Using the FLUX2D and FEMM Software
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents the results of the numerical modeling of the induction heating process using two commercial software. It also analyses the results of simulations performed with the help of the two commercial software, i.e. Flux2D and FEMM 4.2, for the tempering process of a semifinished product.

Author Keywords: the electromagnetic field coupled with the magnetic field

articleTitle: Management of the Electric Energy Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is the management of the power distribution network taking into account the number of the not energized network points and the duration of every incident or the total duration of all incidents. Therefore, it is necessary to adapt the power distribution network management from the generation of the electrical power to the consumers (by delivering without outage the requested power). By following the above mentioned strategy it is necessary the electricity network planning and its operation so as to prioritize the new vulnerabilities of the grid in terms of electricity outages and incidents of consumers. The criterion is to identify overloaded points and eliminate them such that the outages are avoided. The main purpose is the consumer satisfaction. The power flow is only a tool for estimating network elements, this estimation being the authentic method of analyzing the efficiency of the power distribution network management.

articleTitle: Surface scanning device using ultrasound transducers
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This article presents a low-cost equipment used for surface scanning. The proposed scanner uses the ultrasound technique. There are several types of devices for scanning using the ultrasound technique, such as sonar or the echography. The solution proposed in this paper it is intendent to be low cost and differs from other scanning possibilities through the presentation of the results, the scanning mode and the introduction of the scan error correction.

articleTitle: Determining the Potential for Recovery, Reuse and Recycling of Construction and Demolition Waste Assisted by High Frequency Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Construction and demolition projects are large waste generators, being a sensitive issue for any EU country that has to comply with Directive 2008/98 / EC, recycling of which is a subject of global interest. In this work demolition waste resulted from both civilian and industrial residential complexes was considered. The most important milestone was the identification of waste (wood, concrete, masonry, gypsum, granular waste (ballast, sand), iron etc.) in order to focus on recycling. The experiments performed showed that, in the demolition stages, concrete wastes are the most important and have the largest volume accounting for 57.3 % of the total waste of a building. Identifying methods for reducing waste resulting from construction through recovery, reuse and recycling will increase the percentage of green buildings and give a boost to the stagnant construction market since the last global crisis. In this work, a series of laboratory tests were performed using the high frequency electromagnetic field to determine the performance properties of the identified materials to assess their potential use.

articleTitle: Extracting Essential Oils from the Rosehips in the Microwave Field
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The main objective of this work was to find a solution for the extraction of essential oils of rosehip fruits by means of microwaves without affecting its biological properties. During the experiments it was observed that with the diminishing of the size of the experimental material, the microwave power decreased, and the amount of oil increased, with a very good quality of its properties.

articleTitle: Organizing Committee
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: mobile robots; microwave heating; carbon compounds; electromagnetic fields; drying; traffic engineering computing; separation; silicon compounds; optimisation; product quality.

articleTitle: The study of inhomogeneities effect on the insulation of a power cable
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The paper deals with the 3D numerical modeling of the electric field within a power cable whose polyethylene insulation have inhomogeneities. Two types of inhomogeneities were taken into account: material impurity and gas filled cavity. The influence of physical properties, shape and geometrical dimensions of inhomogeneities on the electric field strength is analyzed. The maximum values of electric field obtained through simulations are compared to a reference value. Starting from a structural analysis of cable insulation, this study can be used in a thorough evaluation of electric field in order to prevent the power cable ageing or breakdown.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Quality management system in the Matlab software
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The PDCA cycle imposed by the ISO 9000 Quality Standard [10] suggests a control loop in automation. The authors have innovatively implemented this cycle in the MATLAB software, finding a common ground between automation with quality control. The production lines have, in addition to the final check required by the PDCA cycle, intermediate checks so that a product that will anyway be inconsistent can be removed from the production line. This saves manpower, energy and machinery loads. The quality management system has been functionally implemented and tested in the MATLAB -Simulink modeling and simulation environment.

articleTitle: Measurements with a Quad Band Field Monitor System for UMTS, LTE and WLAN Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: In this paper, a field measurements monitor system is presented together with a set of measurements. The discussed methodology use an quad-band electric field probe implemented with an antenna. The field monitor is usually installed outdoor, it is equipped with an autonomous power unit and powered jointly by a rechargeable internal battery and directly by solar panels. Four frequency range are available for measurement in real time, day and night, and it covers EGSM, UMTS, LTE and WLAN bands. The presented system is compact in size, simple in design and from anywhere accessible via internet connection. The measured results are in good agreement with theoretical estimations.

articleTitle: An Adjustable Integrated Inductive Capacitive Component to Compensate Reactive Power
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: The following paper presents an integrated inductive capacitive component via its electric equivalent and examines its suitability to provide reactive power to compensate both lagging as well as a leading phase shift for varying loads in the power system. Explaining the functional concepts of the integrated component shows how its terminal impedance can be adjusted to be both capacitive and inductive. A specially constructed pilot arrangement demonstrates how this component can provide via a specific regulation process the exact capacitive reactive power to compensate the phase shift caused by an induction motor in an elementary one source single phase domestic voltage supply circuit. The same pilot arrangement is further being adjusted to provide exact inductive reactive power to compensate the phase shift of a capacitive load. Calculations and appropriate measurements verify the concept of the dual character of the component. Extended preliminary experimentation to be pursued further indicate at this stage reasonable prospects for the integrated component to regulate the phase shift automatically maintaining thus a constant predetermined desired value.

Author Keywords: electrical equivalent of wound aluminum foils

articleTitle: Vehicle-Integrated Photovoltaic Modules - Design Considerations and Control Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Photovoltaic modules have become a lot cheaper lately and this makes them extremely attractive for the transportation market. Integrating photovoltaics into transportation vehicles contributes to lower fuel consumption and CO2 emissions, as well as reduced costs. The main purpose of this paper is to show a viable way of integrating photovoltaics into truck trailers, with respect to the efficiency, cost reduction and optimization of the whole process. We propose a series of algorithms and control structures for the PV micro-grids, which can cope better with the specific disturbances and offer better predictability. We also provide a way of estimating the power generated through the use of photoresistors.

articleTitle: Assesment Procedures of the Magnetic Flux Null Value Through a Magnetic Circuit Branch
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: This paper presents a new efficient installation, used to determine the static B-H relationships or even static hysterezis cycles. The functioning principle resembles to the Wheatstone bridge. A most important aspect for the accuracy of the measurements made with this device is the control of the magnetic flux null value through the median yoke. Some control procedures are presented.

Author Keywords: estimation of the magnetic flux null value

articleTitle: Discrete Modeling and Control of an Industrial Robot used in a Metallurgical Process
publicationTitle: 2019 15th International Conference on Engineering of Modern Electric Systems (EMES)
abstract: Industrial robots are used in a variety of industry branches, especially where precision is needed. This paper deals with modeling and control of a positioning process for an industrial robot part of the hot rolling chain, that must extract with accuracy heated billets from a rotary hearth furnace. The model is a discrete one, obtained from a continuous form, by using some digitizing methods and different values of sampling time. The authors used Zero-order hold method, simple and Tustin substitutions. The best fitted model is obtained by comparing root means square deviation for each resulted discrete model. The proposed control is a discrete PI control law, implemented and validated using computer simulation software. The parameters result quite easily from closed loop Ziegler Nichols method, but require further tuning to improve transient response performances.
